name: Dahab
tagline: Egypt's laid-back answer to Sharm El Sheikh, a former Bedouin fishing village turned shore-diving and freediving hub on the Gulf of Aqaba.
highlight: Sitting cross-legged on cushions at a seafront camp in Masbat, watching the sun rise pink over the Gulf of Aqaba after an early dive.
shortDescription: Egypt's laid-back Red Sea diving town, a former Bedouin fishing village built around house-reef diving, the legendary Blue Hole and a famously relaxed backpacker pace.
metaDescription: A Dahab travel guide: the Blue Hole, the Canyon, the lagoon, Masbat's seafront cafés, diving and freediving, food and how to plan a visit.
nearestAirport: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport (SSH), about 1.5 hours by road
knownFor: The Blue Hole, house-reef diving, a laid-back backpacker pace
budget: E£1,000–2,500 per day, budget to mid-range

image.alt: The coastal town of Dahab on the Gulf of Aqaba

intro: Dahab is genuinely Egypt's laid-back answer to Sharm El Sheikh, a former Bedouin fishing village strung along the Gulf of Aqaba about an hour and a half up the Sinai coast.
Its reputation rests genuinely on house-reef diving — walking straight off the shore into some of the Red Sea's best diving and freediving, including the legendary, genuinely notorious Blue Hole.
Life here genuinely moves at a different pace than Sharm's resort strip, built around cushion-strewn seafront cafés, budget guesthouses and a close-knit diving and freediving community.

whyVisit.intro: Dahab's case rests genuinely on world-class shore diving paired with an unusually relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere.

points.title: The diving here is genuinely shore-based and exceptional
points.text: Walk straight off the beach into reef walls that would require a boat almost anywhere else.

points.title: It's genuinely one of the world's great freediving hubs
points.text: Multiple international freediving schools and a calm, deep bay draw the discipline's top athletes.

points.title: The pace here is genuinely far more relaxed than Sharm
points.text: A backpacker, Bedouin-influenced town with no big resort strip to speak of.

points.title: The lagoon is genuinely excellent for windsurfing and kitesurfing
points.text: Flat, shallow water and reliable wind make it a genuine watersports draw.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a quieter Red Sea base
points.text: Easily combined with Sharm El Sheikh or a wider Sinai itinerary.

attractionsIntro: Dahab's essential sights are genuinely centred on its famous dive sites and its laid-back seafront.

attractions.name: The Blue Hole

image.alt: The Blue Hole dive site near Dahab

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the world's most famous — and most notorious — dive sites, a sinkhole dropping more than 100 metres just off the shore.
attractions.tip: Genuinely only dive here with a qualified local guide and well within your certification level; the site has a serious accident history.

attractions.name: The Canyon

image.alt: The bay at Dahab's Canyon dive site

attractions.text: Genuinely a dramatic underwater crevice a short way up the coast, its narrow walls opening onto a sandy floor around 30 metres down.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a rewarding, slightly easier alternative to the Blue Hole for certified divers.

attractions.name: Dahab's lagoon

image.alt: The shallow lagoon south of Dahab

attractions.text: Genuinely a shallow, sheltered bay just south of town, its flat water and steady wind making it one of the Red Sea's best windsurfing and kitesurfing spots.
attractions.tip: Genuinely beginner lessons are easy to arrange right at the lagoon's watersports centres.

attractions.name: Masbat and Mashraba promenade

image.alt: The seafront promenade at Masbat in Dahab

attractions.text: Genuinely Dahab's social heart, a seafront strip of cushion-scattered restaurants and cafés facing the Gulf of Aqaba.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive for sunrise — the town faces east across the water toward Saudi Arabia's mountains.

attractions.name: Eel Garden

image.file: File:CIMG2630 Galzins Garden Eel at Eel Garden, Dahab, Egypt (2693641328).jpg
image.alt: Garden eels at Dahab's Eel Garden dive and snorkel site

attractions.text: Genuinely a shallow, easy shore dive and snorkel site named for its colony of garden eels swaying from the sandy bottom.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a good site for beginners and underwater photographers alike.

attractions.name: Ras Abu Galum Protected Area

image.alt: The coastline at Ras Abu Galum Protected Area near Dahab

attractions.text: Genuinely a remote Bedouin village and marine reserve reachable only by camel or boat along the coast north of Dahab.
attractions.tip: Genuinely go on an organised camel trek that includes snorkelling stops along the way.

attractions.name: The Coloured Canyon

image.alt: The Coloured Canyon inland from Dahab

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking slot canyon inland toward Nuweiba, its walls streaked red, purple and gold by mineral deposits.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a popular full-day desert excursion, often paired with a Bedouin lunch.

thingsToDoIntro: Dahab genuinely rewards a slower pace, built around diving, watersports and simply relaxing by the water.

thingsToDo.title: Dive the Blue Hole with a qualified guide

image.alt: Diving at the Blue Hole near Dahab

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely bucket-list dive for the qualified, best done early morning with a reputable local dive centre.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely stick to depths well within your certification — the site's notoriety is well earned.

thingsToDo.title: Try freediving
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely major draw for Dahab, home to some of the world's top freediving schools and a calm, deep bay perfect for training.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely beginner courses are widely available and need no prior experience.

thingsToDo.title: Windsurf or kitesurf the lagoon
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely reliable watersports session, the lagoon's flat water and steady wind suiting beginners and experts alike.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely lessons and equipment rental are easy to arrange right at the lagoon.

thingsToDo.title: Snorkel the Eel Garden

image.file: File:CIMG2630 Galzins Garden Eel at Eel Garden, Dahab, Egypt (2693641328).jpg
image.alt: Snorkelling over garden eels at Dahab's Eel Garden

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy, rewarding shore snorkel, drifting over a colony of garden eels and healthy coral.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely rent gear from any of the dive shops lining the promenade.

thingsToDo.title: Take a camel or jeep safari into the desert
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely classic Dahab excursion, riding out toward the mountains or the Coloured Canyon with a Bedouin guide.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely sunset or sunrise trips are the most atmospheric time to go.

thingsToDo.title: Watch sunrise over the Gulf of Aqaba

image.alt: Sunrise over the Gulf of Aqaba at Dahab

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely lovely, easy ritual, the town's east-facing coast turning the water pink before the day's heat sets in.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely grab a coffee from a promenade café and watch from a cushioned seafront seat.

foodIntro: Dahab's food scene genuinely reflects its backpacker, Bedouin-influenced character, relaxed and inexpensive.

foods.name: Fresh grilled Red Sea seafood
foods.text: Genuinely a Dahab staple, fish grilled simply and served right along the promenade.
foods.whereToTry: Seafront restaurants throughout Masbat and Mashraba.

foods.name: Bedouin tea
foods.text: Genuinely a Dahab ritual, sweet tea brewed with fresh herbs and served on cushions at a seafront camp.
foods.whereToTry: Any of the promenade's Bedouin-style seafront cafés.

foods.name: Koshari

image.alt: Koshari, Egypt's national dish of rice, lentils and pasta

foods.text: Genuinely available at Egyptian-run restaurants throughout town, a comforting, filling staple.
foods.whereToTry: Local restaurants away from the busier promenade strip.

foods.name: Ful medames

image.alt: Ful medames, a traditional Egyptian fava bean breakfast

foods.text: Genuinely a traditional, hearty breakfast, found at cafés throughout Dahab.
foods.whereToTry: Local cafés, especially around the older Masbat quarter.

foods.name: Taameya (Egyptian falafel)
foods.text: Genuinely Egypt's own fava-bean falafel, a reliable, inexpensive staple.
foods.whereToTry: Street stalls and restaurants throughout town.

foods.name: Fresh fruit juice
foods.text: Genuinely a refreshing staple after a day of diving, blended fresh at juice bars along the promenade.
foods.whereToTry: Juice bars and cafés throughout Masbat.

accommodation.intro: Dahab genuinely favours simple, characterful stays over big resorts, from budget dive camps to boutique guesthouses.

areas.name: Masbat
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely central, with the widest choice of restaurants and dive centres
areas.text: Genuinely the liveliest stretch of the promenade, easy walking distance to everything.

areas.name: Mashraba and Asalah
areas.bestFor: A genuinely quieter, more local stay a short walk from the main strip
areas.text: Genuinely popular with longer-staying divers and freedivers.

options.text: Genuinely the way most visitors get around central Dahab.

bestTime.headline: March to May and September to November for the most comfortable conditions
bestTime.summary: Dahab is genuinely a year-round destination, with warm water even in the cooler months.

seasons.text: Genuinely comfortable temperatures for diving, freediving and desert excursions alike.
Genuinely similarly excellent conditions, with warm water and fewer crowds than summer.
Genuinely hot on land, though the water stays pleasant and windsurfing conditions are strong.
Genuinely mild and popular with visitors escaping colder climates, though desert nights can turn cold.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Dahab's genuinely warm Red Sea waters make it workable year-round.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Dahab visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely with a reputable, qualified dive centre, especially for the Blue Hole.
Bring genuinely your own certification card if you're a qualified diver.
Pack genuinely reef-safe sunscreen and modest clothing for walking through town.
Never dive genuinely beyond your certification level, whatever a dive guide suggests.
Carry genuinely cash — many smaller promenade restaurants and shops don't take cards.
Bargain genuinely and politely for camel treks and jeep safaris arranged independently.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Dahab?
faq.a: Three to five days genuinely allows time to dive multiple sites and simply enjoy the relaxed pace.

faq.q: Is the Blue Hole as dangerous as its reputation suggests?
faq.a: Its accidents are genuinely almost always tied to divers going beyond their training; with a qualified guide and sensible limits, it's a well-managed dive.

faq.q: Do you need to be a certified diver to visit?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — snorkelling, beginner courses and freediving taster sessions are all widely available.

faq.q: How does Dahab compare to Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.a: Genuinely much more laid-back and budget-friendly, with shore diving replacing Sharm's bigger resort strip and boat-based diving.

faq.q: Can you combine Dahab with Sharm El Sheikh?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — they're about 1.5 hours apart by road, often combined in one Red Sea trip.
Yes, genuinely — windsurfing, kitesurfing, desert excursions and simply relaxing on the promenade all make for a worthwhile stay.
